questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic offer of courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some information was easy, other information not very easy, f.ex. finding the right place to register for codisce fiscale.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some assistance from professors, coordinators and classmates

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. I used "Camplus", but it was a little expensive and very far from the campus (50 min by public transport). They have some very close options to the campus but you need to sign up very quickly.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very recommendable to live closer to the campus, even if its a little more expensive, because it does affect your quality of life as a student having to transport for many hours a day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not many options and/or very expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We can assist classes for one or two weeks before registering. This is nice because we can see if we like them before commiting to them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help from professors/coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'd say explore many classes even in different departments. Sometimes you can find more interesting/aligned options to what you want to learn.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most courses were adequate for the level. In some of them some background was needed to understand most of the topics, but it was ok, professors were helpful if you didnt understand something.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I consider the style of teaching at UCPH to be more relaxed and at the same time organized.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Recycle and Life Cycle Assessment of products and processes
Bioeconomy: management, assessment and intellectual property
Laboratoy in sustainability of livestock systems
Laboratory in sustainability of water management
Laboratory in sustainability of agricultural mechanization

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Life Cycle Assessment was probably my favorite and something that I might use in my professional life in the future. It is very practical and at the same time useful for people interested in a sustainability career.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any sports club because they have some but are not of my interest.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many cultural events around the campus area, like music, theater, sports, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In the academic email we received many invitations to free events, so I'd recommend to join those.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Milan is an amazing city full of museums, food, cafes, parks, streets, etc. I'd recommend to go around the city doing as much as you can. But another amazing thing about Milan is that is close to other amazing cities like Lago di Como, Verona, etc. So, going outside and visit nature, do hikings, explore other cities around Italy is also easy and not so expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, but it had some challenges to understand the cultural context.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Rent in a dorm/appartment where you can meet other people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was a little difficult for me to understand at first.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How laid-back italian culture is. They do not take seriousley many things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-Rent a room close to the campus
-Explore the city as much as you can
-Be open for other classes outside your deparment

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be proactive with your classes and ask about the exams well in advance. You can prepare some exams maybe even in the first months of the semester, so this can save you a lot of time and stress in the last exam weeks.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a very different place, submerging in the culture, learning to adapt, and enjoying the contrasts.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to learn italian (it is mandatory to graduate) at the same time as having other 5 classes and having to plan the thesis as well. It was really challenging to manage all these activities and because of this, I did not have a lot of time to do social stuff.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
